record.original_question: For which minor-closed graph families can the genus be computed in polynomial time?

evidence.quote: Question 9.2 For which minor-closed families of graphs can the genus be calculated in polynomial time?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A class $\mathcal{F}$ of finite simple graphs is called minor-closed if, whenever $G \in \mathcal{F}$ and $H$ is obtained from $G$ by a sequence of vertex deletions, edge deletions, and edge contractions, then $H \in \mathcal{F}$. The (orientable) genus $\gamma(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the minimum integer $g \geq 0$ such that $G$ admits a cellular embedding into the orientable surface $S_g$ of genus $g$. Computing $\gamma(G)$ for an arbitrary input graph $G$ is NP-hard.

Characterize the minor-closed families $\mathcal{F}$ of graphs for which there exists an algorithm that, given $G \in \mathcal{F}$, computes $\gamma(G)$ in time polynomial in $|V(G)|$.
artifact.status_search_result: Computing the genus of a graph is NP-hard in general, and only fixed-parameter or approximation results are known (e.g., linear-time embeddability into a fixed surface, EPTAS for dense graphs). No general characterization of polynomial-time-tractable minor-closed families for genus computation appears in the literature, and the question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Efficient polynomial-time approximation scheme for the genus of dense graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Computing the genus of a graph is one of the fundamental problems in topological graph theory; it is NP-hard, and recent work provides an EPTAS for dense graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Exact polynomial-time genus computation is not known in general; only approximation/fixed-parameter results exist.

status_evidence.title: Graph minor - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: For most minor-closed families, no explicit membership algorithm is known.
status_evidence.claim: Algorithmic questions about minor-closed families remain largely open beyond fixed-parameter regimes.
